# SBP Studio 0.5.0 — optional NVIDIA CUDA acceleration (CuPy)
#
# Install on TOP of requirements.txt, ONLY in the build environment used to
# produce the CUDA variant of the packaged app:
#
#     pip install -r requirements.txt
#     pip install -r requirements-cuda.txt
#
# IMPORTANT — use the [ctk] extra so the wheel pulls the CUDA Toolkit runtime
# libraries (cudart, nvrtc, cuBLAS, cuFFT, …) as self-contained pip packages
# (nvidia-*-cu12). This is what makes a *packageable* CuPy: a bare
# `pip install cupy-cuda12x` (or a conda cupy without cudatoolkit) leaves CuPy
# loading CUDA DLLs from a system/CUDA_PATH location that is NOT present inside
# a frozen .exe, so the bundled app reports "GPU not available". The [ctk]
# wheels place the DLLs under site-packages/nvidia/**/bin, which the packaging
# .spec then collects into the bundle.
#
# Pick the wheel that matches the CUDA driver line on the TARGET machines:
#   * cupy-cuda12x → CUDA 12.x / 13.x drivers   (default below)
#   * cupy-cuda11x → CUDA 11.x drivers
#
# The application detects CuPy at import time and falls back silently to the
# CPU path when no compatible GPU/driver is present (see core/_backends.py),
# so the CUDA build still runs on machines without an NVIDIA GPU — it simply
# does not accelerate. The packaging .spec bundles CuPy only when SBP_BUILD_CUDA=1.

cupy-cuda12x[ctk]
